name: Leander
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Leander, TX 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Leander, TX: the Old Town Christmas Festival and parade, Holidays with the Horses, free Santa photos and library cocoa.
lede: Leander celebrates Christmas in Old Town, where the Chamber and the city run a full day festival that ends with a 60 foot tree, and around town with horses, Santa photos and library sing-alongs.
celebrates: The Leander Chamber of Commerce and the City of Leander host the Old Town Christmas Festival around 100 N Brushy Street, with the Rudolph Run, a Christmas marketplace, a hometown parade, pictures with Santa and the lighting of the city's 60 foot tree, followed by a holiday movie in the park. Open My World Therapeutic Riding Center invites families to Holidays with the Horses. Hyundai of Leander offers free photos with Santa, and Leander Public Library hosts cookies, cocoa and holiday sing-alongs.
lastyear: In 2025 the Old Town Christmas Festival took place on Saturday, December 6, hosted by the Leander Chamber of Commerce and the city and presented by Hyundai of Leander. The city calendar listed the Old Town Rudolph Run, a Christmas Marketplace, pictures with Santa and live performances. The Holiday Community Parade stepped off at 1 pm, and at 6:30 pm families gathered at the future site of Old Town Park to light the 60 foot tree and watch The Grinch with hot chocolate.
facts: Leander was established in 1882 on land sold by the Austin and Northwestern Railroad, and it was named for Leander "Catfish" Brown, a railroad official who helped finish the line. The older town of Bagdad sat about a mile west and faded once the tracks passed it by. To honor that history, the Leander Chamber started the Trail of Trains, painted concrete trains placed around town, with the first one outside the Visitors Center on North Brushy Street.
trains: Trains made Leander. The Austin and Northwestern Railroad founded the town in 1882, and today Leander is the last stop on the CapMetro Red Line, station 10 of 10 on a 32 mile line into downtown Austin, the only stop outside Austin city limits. Kids can hunt for the painted concrete trains on the Leander Trail of Trains with the Chamber's photo scavenger hunt. The Austin Steam Train Association runs the North Pole Flyer from the 1912 Bertram Depot. Amtrak's Texas Eagle stops in Austin, Taylor and San Marcos.

kidfact: Leander was named for a railroad man nicknamed Catfish. Today the town has painted concrete trains all over, and if you find them all for the scavenger hunt, the Visitors Center gives you a prize.
faq: Where is the Leander Christmas tree lighting?

The tree lighting is part of the Old Town Christmas Festival, hosted by the Leander Chamber of Commerce and the City of Leander in Old Town around 100 N Brushy Street. The city lights a 60 foot Christmas tree in the evening and then shows a holiday movie in the park. Check the city festival page for this year's schedule.
Is there a Christmas parade in Leander?

Yes. The Holiday Community Parade is part of the Old Town Christmas Festival and runs through Old Town in the afternoon, after the morning Rudolph Run. In 2025 it stepped off at 1 pm. The rest of the day includes a Christmas marketplace, pictures with Santa, live performances and local food and craft vendors.
Can kids ride a train in Leander?

Yes. Leander station is the last stop of the CapMetro Red Line, so families can ride the commuter train to downtown Austin to see the lights. For a holiday train, the Austin Steam Train Association runs the North Pole Flyer from the 1912 Bertram Depot, about a half hour drive northwest, with unlimited hot chocolate.
What is the Leander Trail of Trains?

It is a set of painted concrete trains placed at landmarks and businesses around Leander, started from an idea by the 2017 Leadership Leander class. The first train, Texas Starry Night, sits at the Chamber and Visitors Center on North Brushy Street. Families can pick up a photo scavenger hunt brochure and earn a prize.

The Texas State Historical Association says Leander began in 1882 when the Austin and Northwestern Railroad laid out a town about a mile east of Bagdad. It was named for Leander "Catfish" Brown, a railroad official, or possibly for station manager Karl Leander. The railroad still shapes the town through the Red Line station.

Rally the corgi has sniffed out the best Christmas events for kids in Leander for 2026, and here is what he found: 4 family events, 3 of them free. The magic runs from Saturday, December 5 through Saturday, December 19, with the Old Town Christmas Festival (Saturday, December 5), Holidays with the Horses at Open My World Therapeutic Riding Center (December 11 and 12) and Free Photos with Santa at Hyundai of Leander (Saturday, December 19). New in this update: Holidays with the Horses (December 11 and 12), Free Photos with Santa at Hyundai of Leander (December 19) and Cookies and Cocoa and Holiday Sing-Along at Leander Public Library (December 9 and 10). We check every date on the host's own website, and each listing links straight there. For the rest of the state, see our Texas Christmas events for kids guide.

Planning a bigger day out? Leander families also use our guide to Christmas events for kids in Austin, which covers the Austin Trail of Lights, the Zilker Holiday Tree, the North Pole Flyer train ride and dozens of free family events across the area.

  • Also on the list: a library cocoa and sing-along and a lights evening at a therapeutic riding center
